title: Stepped-wedge trial: the Hussey-Hughes mixed model
summary: The intervention effect in a stepped-wedge cluster trial, from a linear mixed model with period fixed effects and a random intercept per cluster.
pinned_defaults: Both: period as FIXED effects (factor(period) / C(period)). Without them the secular trend is credited to the intervention: on this fixture +1.22 against -1.56.

Python: the intervention SE computed as lme4 reports it, (X'V^-1 X)^-1 conditional on the REML variance components. statsmodels' bse inverts the joint Hessian and differed by 1.8e-5; the conditional form is the standard one and the basis of Kenward-Roger.

Python: the optimizer starts from a moment estimate of the ward variance. From statsmodels' default start, CI (Linux, Python 3.12) reached the zero-variance boundary on this fixture while macOS reached the optimum.

Python: tight L-BFGS settings, and the 'Random effects covariance is singular' warning (raised when an optimizer iterate touches the boundary) silenced with an assertion that the FINAL ward variance is positive.
_few_clusters: With 12 wards the Wald interval is too narrow. Report a Kenward-Roger or Satterthwaite interval (lmerTest), or randomization inference over the possible rollout orders. This entry's Wald interval is the cross-language baseline, not the recommended final interval.
